# @effect-libs/browser

> Browser automation for Cloudflare Workers and other edge runtimes, built on
> [Effect](https://effect.website) v4. Connect to any browser that supports
> Chrome DevTools Protocol — Steel, Browserbase, Cloudflare Browser Run,
> local Chrome — and get auto-cleanup on success, error, timeout, or
> cancellation.

This file indexes every doc page, every source tree (the authoritative API
reference, in JSDoc), and every runnable example. Give it to an LLM as a
single-shot orientation when working with the library.

In-repo links are relative; source-tree directory links and external links
are absolute (raw fetches cannot resolve a directory, and external pages
have no relative base).

The full API surface is documented as JSDoc on `src/`. Each package's source
tree is the authoritative reference; the markdown docs are narrative,
concepts, recipes, and matrices.

## Source (authoritative API reference, in JSDoc)

- [@effect-libs/browser](https://github.com/LordCoughmann/effect-libs-browser/tree/main/packages/browser/src): core — `BrowserProvider` interface, shared types, `FetchSchemas`, error helpers
- [@effect-libs/browser-playwright](https://github.com/LordCoughmann/effect-libs-browser/tree/main/packages/browser-playwright/src): full Playwright API on edge runtimes; **stable**
- [@effect-libs/browser-stagehand](https://github.com/LordCoughmann/effect-libs-browser/tree/main/packages/browser-stagehand/src): AI-powered browser automation (Stagehand v3); **stable**
- [@effect-libs/browser-cdp](https://github.com/LordCoughmann/effect-libs-browser/tree/main/packages/browser-cdp/src): zero-dependency, native-WebSocket CDP client; **experimental**
- [@effect-libs/browser-providers](https://github.com/LordCoughmann/effect-libs-browser/tree/main/packages/browser-providers/src): Steel, Browserbase, Cloudflare Browser Run (HTTP and binding) providers

## Modules

### `@effect-libs/browser-playwright` (stable)

- [browser-playwright](docs/modules/playwright/index.md): landing page, install, runtime compatibility, when to use
- [browser-playwright — Context API](docs/modules/playwright/context.md): `BrowserContext` wrapper, context vs page vs connection
- [browser-playwright — Added APIs](docs/modules/playwright/added-apis.md): `page.fetch`, `page.httpClient`, `page.context()`, lazy getters
- [browser-playwright — Errors](docs/modules/playwright/errors.md): typed reason hierarchy, module-field table
- [browser-playwright — Comparison & Alternatives](docs/modules/playwright/comparison.md): vs other libraries

### Stagehand (stable)

- [browser-stagehand](docs/modules/stagehand/index.md): landing, install, `ws` polyfill for Workers, schema conversion errors
- [browser-stagehand — Errors](docs/modules/stagehand/errors.md): 3-reason table, `SchemaConversionError`, `agent` discussion
- [browser-stagehand — Comparison & Alternatives](docs/modules/stagehand/comparison.md): vs other libraries, design rationale

### `@effect-libs/browser-cdp` (experimental)

- [browser-cdp](docs/modules/cdp/index.md): landing, capabilities matrix, AI / LLM usage disclosure
- [browser-cdp — Locators](docs/modules/cdp/locators.md): `CdpLocator` deep dive
- [browser-cdp — Network](docs/modules/cdp/network.md): network interception, fetch, cookies, storage
- [browser-cdp — Context API](docs/modules/cdp/context.md): context vs page, `withContext` vs `withPage` tradeoffs
- [browser-cdp — Event Streams](docs/modules/cdp/streams.md): event streams (console, network, page events)
- [browser-cdp — Frames](docs/modules/cdp/frames.md): frames, `CdpFrame`, `CdpFrameLocator`, frame selectors
- [browser-cdp — Evaluate](docs/modules/cdp/evaluate.md): `page.evaluate`, no-imports payload constraint, return-value serialization
- [browser-cdp — Handles](docs/modules/cdp/handles.md): `CdpHandle`, `evaluateHandle`, `callFunctionOn`
- [browser-cdp — Errors](docs/modules/cdp/errors.md): 14-reason table, module-field table
- [browser-cdp — Comparison & Alternatives](docs/modules/cdp/comparison.md): vs other libraries, design rationale

## AI / LLM usage disclosure

The library's architecture (client and provider abstractions, scopes, errors) is designed and coded by the maintainer. The `@effect-libs/browser-cdp` internals — `packages/browser-cdp/src/internal/` — are coded by frontier LLMs under the maintainer's supervision, with over 1,000 integration tests ported directly from upstream Playwright specs and run against live Chrome on every supported runtime. See [the AI / LLM usage disclosure section in the `browser-cdp` landing page](docs/modules/cdp/index.md#ai--llm-usage-disclosure) for the full disclosure, the TDD methodology, and the parity-coverage caveat.
